<description>
The HTTP server frames a request body by Content-Length when its `Transfer-Encoding` is not exactly `chunked`.

`LoadBody()` reads only the first `Transfer-Encoding` header. With `gzip`, `chunked, gzip`, or `identity` followed by a second `chunked` header, the body is read by Content-Length, or not at all. RFC 9112 section 6.3 requires a 400 when chunked is not the final coding. The server supports no other coding. I now accept only a single `chunked`, across all `Transfer-Encoding` headers, and answer anything else with a 400. Unlike #36243, I still allow `Content-Length` next to `chunked`, as the existing `interface_http.py` test expects. The new rejection cases in `httpserver_tests` and `interface_http.py` fail on master and pass with this change. The framing check in the `http_request` fuzz target needed the same change, or it fails on `Transfer-Encoding: chunked, `.

This is one of several PRs from a large audit of Bitcoin Core that I did with the help of LLM tools. The audit produced its evidence all at once, which is why the PRs arrive together. I understand each change fully and will answer review questions myself.
</description>

<commits>
458f88f58e http: reject Transfer-Encoding other than chunked

A request with "Transfer-Encoding: gzip" or "chunked, gzip" is framed
by Content-Length, or read as having no body. So is a request whose
first Transfer-Encoding header is not "chunked". RFC 9112 section 6.3
requires a 400 when chunked is not the final coding. The server
supports no other coding.

LoadBody() now accepts only a single "chunked", across all
Transfer-Encoding headers. Anything else throws, which gives a 400 and
closes the connection. I added unit and functional tests, and updated
the http_request fuzz target to match.
</commits>
